# Story 33 — Knowledge base: articles, categories, publishing and both languages (Story: 524)

## Prerequisites

- Story 2.3 completed: the admin console section pattern (see `backend/app/Modules/Tickets/Http/Controllers/Admin/CategoriesController.php` and `frontend/components/screens/admin/TicketingSection.tsx`) that this story mirrors for **article categories**.
- Story 3.2 completed: the polymorphic attachments subsystem in `backend/app/Modules/Platform/Attachments/*` — new owner type `article` extends `AttachmentOwnerType` (`backend/app/Modules/Platform/Attachments/Domain/AttachmentOwnerType.php`). No new attachment table.
- Coordination with the Tickets module: composer/lookup surfaces must be able to search articles without importing Knowledge domain code (contract only).

---

## Story Goal

Introduce a new **Knowledge** module that owns knowledge articles, per-locale translations, a flat Knowledge-owned category list, and the article lifecycle **Draft → Published → Archived**. Articles carry a **type** label (FAQ, Help article, Solution, Guide), an **internal/public** visibility axis independent of lifecycle, and per-locale translations (`en`, `ar`) as rows in `article_translations`. Publishing sets a **write-once** `has_been_published` flag; delete is allowed only while that flag is false; otherwise archive. Attachments reuse the Platform attachments pipeline. Bodies are sanitised on write to a restricted element/attribute allow-list and escaped on render.

**Out of scope (explicit — do not reintroduce, per intake):** review queue / “In review” state / reviewer role / approval workflow, revision history, draft-of-a-published-article, scheduled publishing, nested subcategories, per-article view counts and helpfulness metrics, and the two consumer entry points (agent-side composer lookup and portal help-centre search) — those belong to their own Epic 8 stories. This story delivers the module, admin CRUD, lifecycle, translations, attachments and audit; it does **not** deliver the ticket-composer article picker or the portal help-centre reader.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Delete** is allowed **only when** `has_been_published = false`. Otherwise the controller returns a problem-details response indicating **Archive** is the available action and why. The UI surfaces which of the two controls is available.
- **Lifecycle:** Draft → Published → Archived. **No** In-review, **no** reviewer, **no** submit-for-review. Direct publish by any user holding `knowledge.publish`.
- **`internal_only` (boolean)** is orthogonal to lifecycle. An article is customer-visible **iff** `internal_only = false AND status = published`. Enforcement lives in the query layer, not the view layer.
- **Types:** enum `faq | help | solution | guide`. Label only. Does not gate permission, delivery, or any other behaviour.
- **Categories:** exactly one per article. Flat list. Managed by administrators through the Knowledge admin section. Distinct table from `ticket_categories`; no FK between them.
- **Translations:** rows in `article_translations(article_id, locale, title, body)`. Locale enum `en | ar`. An Arabic-only article is valid.
- **Language fallback:** reader's locale served when present; otherwise the article's **default locale** (recorded on the article), and the response includes a `served_locale` field so the UI can tell the reader.
- **RTL** rendering in Arabic (already handled by the shell); Gregorian dates and Western digits in both locales (already handled by `frontend/lib/format/*`).
- **Sanitise on write** to a restricted allow-list; escape on render. Both defences required.
- **Audit** publish, archive, delete with actor and timestamp on the article row (`published_at`, `archived_at`, `deleted_at`, `published_by`, `archived_by`, `deleted_by`) **and** through `AuditWriter`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Delete of a published article** — controller returns HTTP 409 with problem-details `type: /problems/article-archive-only`, `code: article.archive_only`, `title: "Published articles cannot be deleted"`. Frontend button is disabled with the same message. Enforcement lives in `ArticleLifecycle::delete()` and the controller returns the domain exception via `ProblemDetailsHandler`.
- **Publish → Archive → Publish** — `has_been_published` remains `true` throughout. `published_at` is overwritten by the second publish; `archived_at` is cleared. Delete stays forbidden forever after the first publish. Verified in `ArticleLifecycleTest`.
- **First-time publish with no translations** — 422 problem-details citing “at least one translation required.” Enforced in `ArticlePublishController` before the state transition.
- **Publish with `default_locale` missing among translations** — 422; the default locale row must exist so the fallback path can serve something.
- **Reader locale absent** — read endpoints (added by later stories, but shape defined here on `ArticleResource`) return `served_locale = default_locale` and include an explanatory field. Never a blank body, never an empty section.
- **Sanitiser strips everything** — if the sanitised body ends up empty (e.g. author pasted only a `<script>` block), respond 422 “Body was empty after sanitisation.” Prevents silent data loss.
- **Attachment on an article whose owner authorisation fails** — signed-URL issuance returns 403 through the existing Platform stream controller; the Knowledge owner-authoriser must return the same problem-details shape.
- **Category deletion with articles attached** — 409 problem-details citing article count. Mirrors `Tickets/Admin/CategoriesController::destroy`.
- **Concurrent edits** — mirror `VersionGuard` pattern from `backend/app/Modules/Tickets/Domain/Concurrency/VersionGuard.php`; articles carry an integer `version` incremented on every write; update requests supply `If-Match` and the controller 409s on stale writes.
- **Removing the default-locale translation** — refused (422) unless the caller also promotes another locale to `default_locale` in the same request.
- **RTL body containing bidi controls** — sanitiser preserves `dir="rtl"` on block-level elements; verify with a fixture in `HtmlSanitiserTest`.
- **Cross-module coupling** — Deptrac (`backend/deptrac.yaml`) must be updated so `Knowledge` may depend on `Platform` (attachments, audit) and `Security` (capabilities) but **not** on `Tickets` or `Customers`. Confirm by running `vendor/bin/deptrac` after wiring.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migrations are additive: two new tables plus a possible enum extension for `AttachmentOwnerType`. Rollback drops the two tables and removes the enum value (grep first — if any row uses `owner_type='article'` the rollback must delete those attachment rows or leave the enum value in place).
- Half-applied state: if `articles` exists but `article_translations` does not, the API layer refuses to boot until both tables are present (guard in `KnowledgeServiceProvider::boot()` checking `Schema::hasTable`).
- Rolling back after any article has been published is safe (no data loss elsewhere) but destructive to knowledge content — require an operator confirmation flag, matching the pattern already used by attachment migrations.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `cd backend && composer install && php artisan migrate --seed && vendor/bin/phpunit --testsuite=Feature --filter=Knowledge`.
2. **Backend architecture:** `cd backend && vendor/bin/phpunit --testsuite=Architecture` and `vendor/bin/deptrac`.
3. **OpenAPI regeneration:** `cd backend && php artisan openapi:generate` — commit the diff; `php artisan openapi:check` passes.
4. **Frontend runs:** `cd frontend && pnpm install && pnpm run api:generate && pnpm test`.
5. **Frontend lint / tokens:** `cd frontend && pnpm lint && pnpm test:tokens`.
6. **Regression:** `cd backend && vendor/bin/phpunit --testsuite=Feature --filter=Attachments` (attachment owner-type change must not break existing owners); `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter=Capabilities`.
7. **Manual smoke:** create an article, add `en` + `ar` translations, upload an attachment, publish, try delete (expect refusal + Archive offered), archive, republish, then try delete again (still refused).
